justification: 13 live DCP rows say in their own words they apply only to land on a classified or State road, but reached every house in their council. New site flags state_road / classified_road from the TfNSW NSW Road Network Categorisation (legal State/Regional class) and the cadastre road corridor the lot touches; gate rules move those rows to the flags.

falsifiable_check.command: cd frontend-nextjs && npx jest __tests__/lib __tests__/api; python -m pytest -q tests/test_gate_rules.py
falsifiable_check.fails_when: A lot one street back is flagged, a lot on a State road is not, a 7xxx regional road counts as classified, or the route serves the rows without the flag.
falsifiable_check.observed_red: Before: the 13 rows were in the generic layer, shown to every house in Ashfield, Leichhardt, City of Sydney, Wollongong, Hornsby and Canterbury-Bankstown.
falsifiable_check.external_authority: TfNSW NSW_Roads_Network_Categorisation_vw FeatureServer layers 0/1 (admin_class S/R, edited 2026-10-03); live lots: 1311 Pacific Hwy state+classified; 30 Marion St Leichhardt classified; 2 Kissing Point Rd (7421) neither; one street back not flagged.

pre_impl.existing_data: Generalises the Part 20 rail/busy-road check (#1417) into lib/lot-adjacency.ts; Part 20 tests still pass.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A centreline-distance test would flag lots one street back from wide roads; the flag requires the lot to touch the road corridor the classified centreline runs inside.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Two flags, one shared adjacency lib, gate rules in a new file (gate_rules.py at the 500-line limit).

functions.name: apply_gate_rules
functions.input: the road gate rules from gate_rules_roads.py for six councils
functions.output: 13 rows moved to condition state_road or classified_road (dry runs)
functions.if_none: zero matching rows means nothing is written for that council

values.value: 3 m adjacency: 12 frontage lots 0-1.51 m from their road corridor; one-back lot has none within 30 m
tsc 0 errors; jest 106 suites / 1437 tests; pytest 27

break_it.scenario: A lot one street back from a highway is flagged.
break_it.what_happens: A house not on the road is shown road-frontage rules.
break_it.how: Flag needs the lot to touch the corridor holding the classified centreline; one-back lot not flagged (test).

break_it.scenario: An unclassified regional road (7xxx) is treated as classified.
break_it.what_happens: Lots on unclassified regional roads would get classified-road rules.
break_it.how: 7000-7999 excluded from classified_road (recorded assumption; schedule PDF blocked).

break_it.scenario: The TfNSW or cadastre service fails at lookup.
break_it.what_happens: The lot's road flags cannot be computed.
break_it.how: No flag and a plain note on the page, as for Part 20.
break_it.repro: route test with the lookup failing

mutation_analysis: Removing the corridor-containment test or the 7xxx exclusion fails the unit tests.

post_merge.db_reset: Yes, AFTER deploy: derive_precinct_keys.py --council <each of ashfield, leichhardt, city_of_sydney, wollongong, hornsby, canterbury_bankstown> --only <road rules> --apply.
post_merge.manual_verify: Live: 1311 Pacific Hwy shows the gated rows for its council; a one-back lot does not.

residual_risk: 7xxx = unclassified is an inference; roads not held as corridors (some motorways/tunnels) are missed; a lot touching only the junction piece of a side street can be flagged.
